rm_diag_ra1_mcq.question_template: Which of the following inputs is SAFE to paste directly into a non-approved external AI tool when performing {workflow_action} as a {role}?
rm_diag_ra1_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} preparing a {document_type} for an upcoming {meeting_type} with {client_name}. You have access to their latest audited financials, an internal risk rating of 'Watch', a draft term sheet, and a publicly available industry report on {industry} trends. You want to use an AI tool to help structure the {document_type} quickly.

options.label: A
options.text_template: The publicly available industry report on {industry} trends, with no client-specific details added.

options.label: B
options.text_template: The client's audited financial statements, since they are already signed off and filed.

options.label: C
options.text_template: The internal risk rating note, because it is only one line of text and unlikely to cause harm.

options.label: D
options.text_template: The draft term sheet, because it has not yet been executed and is therefore not a final document.

rm_diag_ce7_mcq.question_template: An AI tool drafts the following sentence for inclusion in a {document_type}: '{client_name} has consistently demonstrated strong liquidity management, with a current ratio well above industry benchmarks.' What is the most important critical evaluation step before including this in the {document_type}?
rm_diag_ce7_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} who used an approved AI tool to help draft sections of a {document_type} for {client_name} (a fictional client). The AI generated the sentence above based on your abstracted prompt describing the client as 'an {industry} company with stable working capital.' You are about to paste it into the {document_type} for submission to the {meeting_type}.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Verify the claim against the client's actual financial data — confirm the current ratio figure and check it against a credible industry benchmark before including it.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Check that the sentence is grammatically correct and professionally worded before pasting it in.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Ask the AI to regenerate the sentence with more specific language to make it sound more authoritative.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Accept the sentence as accurate because it matches the general description you provided in your prompt.

rm_diag_dd15_task.question_template: An AI tool produced the {document_type} below. Evaluate the quality of the data reasoning and identify any decisions a {role} should NOT make based solely on this output, explaining why.
rm_diag_dd15_task.scenario_template:
AI-generated {document_type}:

'Analysis of your portfolio indicates that clients in the {industry} sector are your lowest-performing segment by revenue contribution. These clients have the highest average cost-to-serve and the lowest product cross-sell ratio. Based on this, it is recommended that you deprioritise {industry} clients in your outreach plan and focus resources on other clients, who show stronger revenue metrics and higher facility utilisation.'

Your task: (1) Identify at least two data reasoning problems or missing considerations in this analysis. (2) Explain what decisions a {role} should not make based solely on this AI output, and why.

rubric_criteria.name: Identification of data reasoning gaps
rubric_criteria.description_template: Learner identifies at least two specific gaps: e.g., the analysis ignores strategic value of {industry} relationships (referrals, tenure, growth potential), does not account for individual client variation within the segment, and may be based on incomplete or point-in-time data.

rubric_criteria.name: Decisions the {role} should not make solely on this output
rubric_criteria.description_template: Learner correctly identifies that the {role} should not deprioritise or reduce service to {industry} clients, reallocate portfolio resources, or make any client-facing decisions based solely on this AI summary — and explains that such decisions require human judgement, relationship context, and management input.

criteria.name: Identification of data reasoning gaps
criteria.description: Learner identifies at least two specific gaps: e.g., the analysis ignores strategic value of retail relationships (referrals, tenure, growth potential), does not account for individual client variation within the segment, and may be based on incomplete or point-in-time data.

criteria.name: Decisions the RM should not make solely on this output
criteria.description: Learner correctly identifies that the RM should not deprioritise or reduce service to retail clients, reallocate portfolio resources, or make any client-facing decisions based solely on this AI summary — and explains that such decisions require human judgement, relationship context, and management input.

rm_diag_sp6_task.question_template: The prompt below was used to prepare for a {meeting_type} but produced a vague, unhelpful response. Diagnose the prompting weaknesses and rewrite it as a stronger prompt that would generate a more useful output for a {role}.
rm_diag_sp6_task.scenario_template:
A {role} used this prompt before a {meeting_type}:

'Help me prepare for a meeting with a client about renewing their loan.'

The AI returned a generic list of 'tips for client meetings' that was not useful for the {role}'s specific situation. The client is a mid-market {industry} company with a $3M working capital facility up for annual review. The {role} wants to anticipate objections, identify upsell opportunities, and prepare 3 tailored talking points about the value the {org_type} has delivered over the past year.

rubric_criteria.name: Diagnosis of prompt weaknesses
rubric_criteria.description_template: Learner correctly identifies at least two specific weaknesses: missing role/persona, no sector or client context, no specific output requested, and no constraints on format or purpose.

rubric_criteria.name: Quality of rewritten prompt
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten prompt includes: a role frame ({role} preparing for renewal), abstracted client context (mid-market {industry}, working capital facility), specific outputs requested (objection anticipation, upsell opportunities, value talking points), and a clear format instruction.

criteria.name: Diagnosis of prompt weaknesses
criteria.description: Learner correctly identifies at least two specific weaknesses: missing role/persona, no sector or client context, no specific output requested, and no constraints on format or purpose.

criteria.name: Quality of rewritten prompt
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt includes: a role frame (RM preparing for renewal), abstracted client context (mid-market construction, working capital facility), specific outputs requested (objection anticipation, upsell opportunities, value talking points), and a clear format instruction.

rm_diag_ri10_mcq.question_template: A {role} wants to use AI to prepare a client intelligence summary before a {meeting_type}. Which approach best demonstrates effective use of AI for relationship intelligence while staying within responsible AI boundaries?
rm_diag_ri10_mcq.scenario_template: You have a {meeting_type} next week with the CEO of {client_name}, a long-standing client. You want to walk in with a sharp understanding of their business context, recent {industry} developments, and potential needs. You have access to publicly available news, the company's published annual report, and your own (sanitised) notes from previous meetings.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Prompt the AI with publicly available information ({industry} news, published annual report excerpts, sector trends) and your sanitised meeting notes to generate a structured pre-{meeting_type} intelligence brief covering business context, likely priorities, and suggested conversation angles.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Paste the client's full CRM record including internal risk ratings and deal history into the AI tool to get the most comprehensive intelligence summary possible.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Ask the AI to generate a client profile from scratch using only the company name, since AI tools have access to up-to-date business databases.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Use the AI to write a summary of the client's financial performance based on figures you recall from internal credit reports, without checking the source.

rm_diag_ac16_mcq.question_template: A {role} uses AI to draft a follow-up email to a client after a difficult conversation about a declined credit application. Which of the following best describes the correct approach to using the AI draft?
rm_diag_ac16_mcq.scenario_template: You had a tense call with the {role} of {client_name} after their facility increase request was declined by the {meeting_type}. You want to send a professional, empathetic follow-up email that acknowledges their disappointment, explains the next steps, and keeps the relationship intact. You use an approved AI tool to draft the email.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Review the AI draft carefully, adjust the tone to reflect your genuine relationship with the {role}, verify that all stated next steps are accurate, and ensure no confidential {meeting_type} reasoning is inadvertently disclosed before sending.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Send the AI draft immediately — it will be more professionally worded than anything you could write quickly, and speed matters after a difficult conversation.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Ask the AI to make the email more persuasive so the client feels the decision was the right one, without changing any factual content.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Use the AI draft as the final version but add the client's name and your signature, since personalisation is sufficient review for a routine follow-up.

uw_diag_ra1_mcq.question_template: Which of the following inputs is safe to include verbatim in a {org_type} approved AI tool prompt without any abstraction or modification?
uw_diag_ra1_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} preparing a {document_type} for a new transaction involving {client_name}. You have four documents available: an internal client file note with payment history and risk commentary, a publicly available trade credit rating report published by a recognised ratings agency, a draft term sheet with proposed covenant thresholds, and an internal memo showing the deal's preliminary risk rating and rationale. You want to use a {org_type} approved AI tool to help structure your analysis.

options.label: A
options.text_template: The publicly available trade credit rating report sourced from the ratings agency's published website.

options.label: B
options.text_template: The internal client file note, because it is stored on {org_type}'s secure internal system.

options.label: C
options.text_template: The draft term sheet, because the deal has not yet been approved and no client has signed it.

options.label: D
options.text_template: The internal risk rating memo, because it contains analytical reasoning rather than raw financial figures.

uw_diag_sp6_task.question_template: Review the prompt below, which a {role} used to draft a covenant analysis section. Identify at least two specific structural weaknesses that reduce the quality of the AI output, and rewrite the prompt to address those weaknesses.
uw_diag_sp6_task.scenario_template:
A {role} submitted the following prompt to your {org_type}'s approved AI tool:

---
"Analyse the covenants for this deal and tell me if they are appropriate."
---

The AI returned a two-sentence response stating that covenants are generally important for credit risk management and that leverage and interest coverage ratios are commonly used. The {role} found this unhelpful. Diagnose the prompt's weaknesses and produce an improved version.

rubric_criteria.name: Diagnosis of prompt weaknesses
rubric_criteria.description_template: Identifies at least two specific structural weaknesses: e.g., no context about the borrower or transaction type, no definition of 'appropriate,' no output format specified, no analytical criteria provided, no role framing, and no abstracted inputs supplied to ground the analysis.

rubric_criteria.name: Quality of rewritten prompt
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten prompt includes role framing or context, specifies the type of transaction and borrower profile (abstracted), defines what 'appropriate' means in {role} terms (e.g., aligned with leverage profile, sector norms), requests a structured output, and includes a constraint on handling missing information.

criteria.name: Diagnosis of prompt weaknesses
criteria.description: Identifies at least two specific structural weaknesses: e.g., no context about the borrower or transaction type, no definition of 'appropriate,' no output format specified, no analytical criteria provided, no role framing, and no abstracted inputs supplied to ground the analysis.

criteria.name: Quality of rewritten prompt
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt includes role framing or context, specifies the type of transaction and borrower profile (abstracted), defines what 'appropriate' means in underwriting terms (e.g., aligned with leverage profile, sector norms), requests a structured output, and includes a constraint on handling missing information.

uw_diag_dd15_task.question_template: Review the AI-generated analysis excerpt below, which was produced to support a credit decision. Identify at least two analytical weaknesses or data reasoning errors that a {role} should correct before relying on this output, and explain what additional analysis or data would be needed.
uw_diag_dd15_task.scenario_template:
A {role} used a {org_type} approved AI tool to analyse an abstracted borrower profile. The AI produced the following excerpt for the 'Financial Assessment' section:

---
"The borrower's revenue has grown at an average of 12% per year over the past three years, indicating strong business momentum. The current ratio of 1.8x suggests adequate short-term liquidity. Based on these indicators, the borrower demonstrates a solid financial profile consistent with investment-grade characteristics. The debt service coverage ratio is not provided but is assumed to be sufficient given the revenue growth trend."
---

rubric_criteria.name: Identification of analytical weaknesses
rubric_criteria.description_template: Identifies at least two specific analytical weaknesses: e.g., revenue growth alone does not indicate creditworthiness without profitability or margin data; 'investment-grade' characterisation is unsupported by the data provided; the DSCR assumption is a hallucinated inference not grounded in any provided figure; the current ratio alone is insufficient to assess liquidity without context on payables, inventory quality, or cash position.

rubric_criteria.name: Additional analysis or data requirements
rubric_criteria.description_template: Identifies what additional data or analysis is needed: e.g., actual DSCR from the financial model, EBITDA margin and net income trends, leverage ratio, cash flow from operations, and sector benchmarks to contextualise the current ratio and growth rate before any creditworthiness conclusion can be drawn.

criteria.name: Identification of analytical weaknesses
criteria.description: Identifies at least two specific analytical weaknesses: e.g., revenue growth alone does not indicate creditworthiness without profitability or margin data; 'investment-grade' characterisation is unsupported by the data provided; the DSCR assumption is a hallucinated inference not grounded in any provided figure; the current ratio alone is insufficient to assess liquidity without context on payables, inventory quality, or cash position.

criteria.name: Additional analysis or data requirements
criteria.description: Identifies what additional data or analysis is needed: e.g., actual DSCR from the financial model, EBITDA margin and net income trends, leverage ratio, cash flow from operations, and sector benchmarks to contextualise the current ratio and growth rate before any creditworthiness conclusion can be drawn.

uw_diag_ce7_mcq.question_template: An AI tool has generated a financial risk summary for a borrower in the {industry} sector. Which of the following responses represents the most appropriate {role} behaviour when reviewing this output before including it in a {document_type}?
uw_diag_ce7_mcq.scenario_template: You used your {org_type}'s approved AI tool to draft the 'Financial Risk' section of a {document_type} for a solar project developer. The AI output states: 'The borrower's debt service coverage ratio of 1.35x is within acceptable range for project finance transactions in this sector, and the leverage profile is consistent with investment-grade issuers.' You do not recall providing the DSCR figure in your prompt, and you know the borrower's actual leverage is higher than investment-grade norms. As the {role} responsible for this {document_type}, you must decide how to proceed.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Verify the DSCR figure against the source financial model, correct the leverage characterisation based on your own analysis, and revise the section before including it in the {document_type}.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Accept the output as a reasonable approximation since AI tools are trained on large datasets and sector benchmarks are likely accurate.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Delete only the leverage sentence and keep the DSCR statement, since one error does not invalidate the rest of the AI-generated content.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Flag the section as 'AI-generated' in the {document_type} so reviewers know to apply their own judgement, without making any changes yourself.

uw_diag_ac16_mcq.question_template: A {role} has used an AI tool to draft a section of a {document_type}. Which of the following practices best reflects responsible and effective use of AI-augmented communication in this context?
uw_diag_ac16_mcq.scenario_template: You have used your {org_type}'s approved AI tool to draft the 'Transaction Overview' section of a {document_type} for a structured trade finance deal. The AI-generated draft is well-written and covers the main structural elements. However, you notice it uses generic language about the guarantee structure that does not accurately reflect the specific risk-sharing arrangement in this deal, and it omits the rationale for {org_type}'s involvement.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Edit the draft to correct the guarantee structure description, add {org_type} mandate rationale, verify all factual claims, and ensure the final section reflects your professional judgement before submitting.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Submit the AI draft as written since it is well-structured and the approval committee will identify any inaccuracies during their review.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Add a footnote stating 'drafted with AI assistance' and submit without changes, as disclosure of AI use satisfies the quality assurance requirement.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Ask the AI to revise the section by providing the correct guarantee structure details, including the specific deal terms, to get a more accurate draft.

uw_diag_ri10_mcq.question_template: A {role} is preparing for a first meeting with a new {org_type} partner to discuss a potential risk-sharing arrangement. Which use of AI is most appropriate for building relationship intelligence ahead of this meeting?
uw_diag_ri10_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} preparing for an introductory meeting with {client_name}, a {org_type} seeking to co-insure a portfolio of export receivables. You have access to the {org_type}'s publicly available annual report, a press release about their recent {industry} expansion, and an internal {document_type} from the deal team. You want to use AI to help you prepare.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Use {org_type}'s approved AI tool to synthesise publicly available information about {client_name}'s {industry} strategy, recent announcements, and regional focus to prepare informed questions and identify potential alignment with {org_type}'s mandate.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Paste the internal deal team {document_type} into a general AI chatbot to generate a relationship summary, since the {document_type} contains the most relevant context for the meeting.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Ask the AI to predict {client_name}'s risk appetite and likely negotiating positions based on their public profile, and treat the output as a reliable basis for your meeting strategy.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Use AI to draft a relationship history summary by asking it to recall previous {org_type} interactions with {client_name} from its training data.

an_diag_ra1_mcq.question_template: Which of the following inputs is safe to include verbatim in an AI assistant prompt without any abstraction or modification?
an_diag_ra1_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} preparing a {industry} sector overview for a {workflow_action}. You have several documents on your desk: an internal credit risk rating memo for a {client_name}, a published annual report from a publicly listed company, a draft strategy document from your team, and a third-party embargoed research report. You need to use an AI assistant to help synthesise background information.

options.label: A
options.text_template: The published annual report of the publicly listed company, sourced from its investor relations website.

options.label: B
options.text_template: The internal credit risk rating memo, because it is already stored in your {org_type}'s secure drive.

options.label: C
options.text_template: The embargoed third-party research report, because it contains sector-level data rather than {client_name}-specific data.

options.label: D
options.text_template: The draft strategy document, because it has not yet been formally classified as confidential.

an_diag_ce7_mcq.question_template: A {role} uses Copilot to generate a summary of {industry} risk indicators for a sector report. Which action best reflects critical evaluation of the AI output before it is used in a client-facing {document_type}?
an_diag_ce7_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} at {org_type}. You used Copilot to generate a paragraph summarising key {industry} risk indicators for the {industry} sector. The output reads fluently and cites what appear to be specific statistics (e.g., 'vacancy rates rose to 18.4% in Q2' and 'debt-service coverage ratios fell below 1.2x for 34% of loans'). You are about to paste this paragraph into a {document_type} that will be shared with clients.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Verify the specific statistics against the original source documents or authoritative databases before including them, and flag any figures that cannot be confirmed.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Accept the output as accurate because Copilot is connected to {org_type} data and would not fabricate statistics.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Lightly edit the paragraph for tone and include it, since the figures are plausible and consistent with general market knowledge.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Ask Copilot to regenerate the paragraph twice more and use the version that appears most consistent across the three outputs.

an_diag_sp6_task.question_template: Review the prompt below submitted by a {role}. Identify its weaknesses as a strategic prompt, then rewrite it to be significantly more effective for the {role}'s stated purpose.
an_diag_sp6_task.scenario_template:
A {role} at {org_type} submitted this prompt to help prepare for a client meeting:

---
"Tell me about the {industry} sector."
---

The {role}'s actual goal was to prepare a five-minute verbal briefing for a {role} who is meeting a mid-sized {industry} company ({client_name}) to discuss potential export financing. The briefing should cover current commodity price trends, key operational risks, and one or two talking points relevant to export financing conversations.

rubric_criteria.name: Weakness diagnosis
rubric_criteria.description_template: Correctly identifies at least two weaknesses in the original prompt: it is too broad/vague, specifies no audience or purpose, defines no output format, and provides no analytical focus or scope.

rubric_criteria.name: Role and context added
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten prompt specifies a role for the AI tool and provides relevant context (e.g., preparing a verbal briefing for a {role} meeting a {industry} company to discuss export financing).

rubric_criteria.name: Format and scope defined
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten prompt specifies the output format (e.g., a concise verbal briefing outline or bullet points) and scope (e.g., commodity price trends, operational risks, export financing talking points).

rubric_criteria.name: Overall improvement in strategic quality
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten prompt is substantially more likely to produce a useful, targeted output than the original — it is specific, purposeful, and calibrated to the {role}'s actual workflow need.

criteria.name: Weakness diagnosis
criteria.description: Correctly identifies at least two weaknesses in the original prompt: it is too broad/vague, specifies no audience or purpose, defines no output format, and provides no analytical focus or scope.

criteria.name: Role and context added
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt specifies a role for Copilot and provides relevant context (e.g., preparing a verbal briefing for a relationship manager meeting a copper mining company to discuss export financing).

criteria.name: Format and scope defined
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt specifies the output format (e.g., a concise verbal briefing outline or bullet points) and scope (e.g., commodity price trends, operational risks, export financing talking points).

criteria.name: Overall improvement in strategic quality
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt is substantially more likely to produce a useful, targeted output than the original — it is specific, purposeful, and calibrated to the analyst's actual workflow need.

an_diag_dd15_task.question_template: Review the AI-generated data interpretation below. Identify any analytical errors, unsupported conclusions, or data reasoning problems, and explain what the {role} should do before using this output in a {meeting_type}.
an_diag_dd15_task.scenario_template:
A {role} asked Copilot to analyse five years of EBITDA margin data for 40 {industry} companies. Copilot returned the following interpretation:

---
'Analysis of the dataset shows that EBITDA margins across the sector have improved steadily by an average of 2.3 percentage points per year over the five-year period. This confirms that the {industry} sector is in a strong growth phase and presents low credit risk overall. Three companies — {client_name}, {client_name}, and {client_name} — show margins significantly below the sector average and should be immediately flagged as high credit risk and removed from the portfolio. The trend is consistent and unlikely to reverse given current macroeconomic conditions.'
---

Your task: Identify all analytical and reasoning problems in this output, and specify what steps the {role} should take before acting on these findings.

rubric_criteria.name: Analytical errors identified
rubric_criteria.description_template: Identifies at least two analytical errors: (1) conflating EBITDA margin improvement with 'low credit risk overall' — margin is one indicator, not a complete credit assessment; (2) the conclusion that below-average margin alone justifies 'high credit risk' and immediate portfolio removal is an unsupported leap; (3) the forward-looking claim about macroeconomic conditions is speculative and unsourced.

rubric_criteria.name: Reasoning problems flagged
rubric_criteria.description_template: Flags that Copilot has made a definitive recommendation (remove companies from portfolio) that exceeds its appropriate role — AI should surface patterns for {role} review, not make portfolio decisions — and that the output presents speculation as certainty.

rubric_criteria.name: Corrective analyst steps specified
rubric_criteria.description_template: Specifies at least two concrete steps the {role} should take before acting: e.g., verify the 2.3pp average figure against the raw data, conduct a fuller credit assessment of the three flagged companies using multiple indicators, and treat the macroeconomic claim as unverified.

criteria.name: Analytical errors identified
criteria.description: Identifies at least two analytical errors: (1) conflating EBITDA margin improvement with 'low credit risk overall' — margin is one indicator, not a complete credit assessment; (2) the conclusion that below-average margin alone justifies 'high credit risk' and immediate portfolio removal is an unsupported leap; (3) the forward-looking claim about macroeconomic conditions is speculative and unsourced.

criteria.name: Reasoning problems flagged
criteria.description: Flags that Copilot has made a definitive recommendation (remove companies from portfolio) that exceeds its appropriate role — AI should surface patterns for analyst review, not make portfolio decisions — and that the output presents speculation as certainty.

criteria.name: Corrective analyst steps specified
criteria.description: Specifies at least two concrete steps the analyst should take before acting: e.g., verify the 2.3pp average figure against the raw data, conduct a fuller credit assessment of the three flagged companies using multiple indicators, and treat the macroeconomic claim as unverified.

an_diag_ac16_mcq.question_template: A {role} uses Copilot to draft a client-facing {document_type}. Which approach best reflects responsible and effective use of AI for professional communication?
an_diag_ac16_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} at {org_type}. Your director has asked you to produce a two-page {document_type} for a corporate client summarising recent developments in the {industry} sector. You use Copilot to generate a first draft based on publicly available sources. The draft is well-structured and reads fluently, but you have not yet reviewed it in detail.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Review the draft carefully for factual accuracy, tone appropriateness, and any claims that need verification or caveating, then edit and personalise it before sending to the client.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Send the Copilot draft directly to the client, since it is based on public sources and reads professionally.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Ask Copilot to review its own draft for errors and send the revised version without further {role} review.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Discard the Copilot draft and write the {document_type} entirely from scratch to ensure full ownership of the content.

an_diag_ri10_mcq.question_template: A {role} is asked to use AI to help prepare a relationship intelligence briefing ahead of a client meeting. Which approach best demonstrates responsible and effective use of AI for this task?
an_diag_ri10_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} at {org_type} supporting a {role} who has a first meeting next week with {client_name}, a mid-sized {industry} company. The {role} wants a {document_type} covering the company's recent business developments, key decision-makers, and any publicly known strategic priorities. You have access to Copilot and a range of public sources.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Use Copilot to synthesise publicly available information (press releases, news articles, published financials) into a structured {document_type}, then verify key facts and add {role} commentary before sharing with the {role}.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Export the client's CRM interaction history and financial exposure data into Copilot to generate a comprehensive {document_type} that includes internal relationship notes.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Ask Copilot to generate a full {document_type} from memory without providing any source documents, since it has broad knowledge of business and industry.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Use Copilot only to format and proofread a {document_type} you have already written manually, since AI should not be involved in {workflow_action} tasks.

mk_diag_ra1_mcq.question_template: Which of the following inputs is SAFE to paste directly into a non-approved external AI tool when drafting a follow-up email campaign as part of a {role}'s {workflow_action}?
mk_diag_ra1_mcq.scenario_template: You attended an industry summit on behalf of your {org_type} and collected a spreadsheet of 200 leads including names, emails, job titles, company names, and conversation notes. As a {role}, you want to use an AI writing tool to help draft a personalised follow-up email series. You also have access to an internal campaign performance report, a publicly available industry outlook on {industry}, and your {org_type}'s approved brand messaging guide (marked 'Internal Use Only').

options.label: A
options.text_template: The publicly available industry outlook on {industry}, referenced only for sector context with no lead details included.

options.label: B
options.text_template: The full lead spreadsheet, because the contacts gave their business cards voluntarily at the event.

options.label: C
options.text_template: The internal campaign performance report, because it contains no client financial data.

options.label: D
options.text_template: The brand messaging guide marked 'Internal Use Only', because it will help the AI match your {org_type}'s tone.

mk_diag_ra2_sandbox.question_template: Write a prompt you would use in an {org_type}'s approved AI tool to draft a follow-up email for {industry} leads — without exposing any personally identifiable or non-public information.
mk_diag_ra2_sandbox.scenario_template: As a {role}, you collected 200 leads at a {industry} trade show. The spreadsheet includes names, emails, job titles, company names, and brief conversation notes. You want to use your {org_type}'s approved AI writing assistant to draft a follow-up email that highlights export financing support for {industry} professionals. You must not include any personal details, real company names, or unpublished internal data in your prompt.

rubric_criteria.name: PII Exclusion
rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt contains no real names, email addresses, company names, or other personally identifiable information from the lead list.

rubric_criteria.name: Contextual Utility
rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt provides enough context (audience type, purpose, key message) for the AI to generate a useful and relevant draft {document_type}.

mk_diag_sp4_mcq.question_template: Which prompting technique would MOST improve the relevance and quality of AI-generated content for a niche audience relevant to a {role}?
mk_diag_sp4_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} developing a content series targeting a specific segment of {industry} professionals at a particular type of organization. You want to use an approved AI writing tool to draft posts that speak directly to this audience's pain points around key financial and operational challenges in the {industry} sector. Your first draft prompt produced generic content that did not resonate with the {industry} context.

options.label: B

mk_diag_ra3_task.question_template: As a {role}, review the AI prompt below and identify all responsible AI problems. Then rewrite the prompt so it is safe to use in a non-approved external AI tool.
mk_diag_ra3_task.scenario_template:
A colleague on your {role} team drafted the following prompt to generate a nurture email:

---
"Here is our lead list from the {client_name} {industry} Expo. Key contacts include [Contact A] ({role}, {client_name}, contact.a@{client_name}.com) and [Contact B] (Export Manager, {client_name}, contact.b@{client_name}.com). Our internal campaign code is AGRI-Q3-2025 and our target conversion rate is 12% (not yet public). Please write a personalised follow-up email for each contact referencing their conversation notes and encouraging them to book a call with our trade advisor."
---

Task: (1) List every responsible AI problem in this prompt. (2) Rewrite the prompt so it is safe to use while still producing a useful email draft.

rubric_criteria.name: Problem Identification — PII
rubric_criteria.description_template: Correctly identifies that real names, email addresses, and {org_type} names are personally identifiable information that should not be entered into a non-approved external AI tool.

rubric_criteria.name: Problem Identification — Non-Public Internal Data
rubric_criteria.description_template: Correctly identifies that the internal campaign code and unpublished conversion rate target are non-public {org_type} data that must not be shared externally.

rubric_criteria.name: Rewrite — PII Removed
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten prompt replaces all real names, emails, and {org_type} names with generic descriptors (e.g. 'a {role} at a mid-sized {industry} exporter') and removes the internal campaign code and conversion figure.

rubric_criteria.name: Rewrite — Utility Preserved
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten prompt still provides sufficient context (audience {role}, {industry}, purpose, desired action) for the AI to generate a useful and relevant follow-up email draft.

criteria.name: Problem Identification — PII
criteria.description: Correctly identifies that real names, email addresses, and company names are personally identifiable information that should not be entered into a non-approved external AI tool.

criteria.name: Problem Identification — Non-Public Internal Data
criteria.description: Correctly identifies that the internal campaign code and unpublished conversion rate target are non-public organisational data that must not be shared externally.

criteria.name: Rewrite — PII Removed
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt replaces all real names, emails, and company names with generic descriptors (e.g. 'a VP of Procurement at a mid-sized grain exporter') and removes the internal campaign code and conversion figure.

criteria.name: Rewrite — Utility Preserved
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt still provides sufficient context (audience role, industry, purpose, desired action) for the AI to generate a useful and relevant follow-up email draft.

rubric_criteria.name: Tone, Format, and CTA in Rewrite
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten prompt specifies tone (warm, professional), word limit (under 200 words), and requests a clear CTA button label.

rubric_criteria.name: Content Direction in Rewrite
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten prompt directs the AI toward the relevant subject matter — trade risk advisory resources — giving the AI enough substance to produce a relevant and useful draft.

mk_diag_ce7_mcq.question_template: An AI tool has generated a statistic for use in a {workflow_action}. What is the MOST appropriate next step before publishing?
mk_diag_ce7_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} who asked an approved AI writing assistant to help draft a thought leadership article on {industry} for a target audience relevant to your {org_type}. The AI produced the following sentence: 'According to recent industry research, 67% of respondents experienced at least one critical disruption in the past 18 months.' You do not recognise this statistic from any source you provided, and the AI did not cite a reference.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Verify the statistic against a credible, traceable source before including it; if no source can be confirmed, remove or replace it with a verified figure.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Keep the statistic because it sounds plausible and aligns with the article's argument.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Add a footnote saying 'Source: AI-generated' so readers know where it came from.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Ask the AI to provide its source, and publish the article once the AI confirms the figure.

mk_diag_ce8_sandbox.question_template: Write a prompt that instructs an AI tool to help you, as a {role}, critically review a draft {document_type} for factual accuracy, brand alignment, and potential bias — before it is published.
mk_diag_ce8_sandbox.scenario_template: Your team has drafted a 600-word {document_type} on the benefits of {industry} for a specific target audience entering new markets. Before publishing, you, as a {role}, want to use an approved AI tool to help you identify any unsupported claims, language that may unintentionally stereotype or exclude, and messaging that may not align with your {org_type}'s inclusive and balanced brand voice. You will still do a final human review, but want AI to flag issues first.

rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt explicitly asks the AI to flag unsupported claims, unverified statistics, or assertions that would require a cited source.

rubric_criteria.name: Bias and Inclusivity Check
rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt asks the AI to identify language that may stereotype, exclude, or unintentionally marginalise any group, particularly given the {document_type}'s focus on the intended audience.

rubric_criteria.name: Brand Voice Alignment
rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt asks the AI to assess whether the tone and messaging align with a defined brand standard (e.g. inclusive, balanced, professional) rather than just asking for general editing.

rubric_criteria.name: Human Review Framing
rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt frames the AI's role as a first-pass reviewer and either explicitly notes that a human will make final decisions or asks the AI to present findings as suggestions rather than corrections.

mk_diag_ri10_mcq.question_template: How should a {role} BEST use AI to prepare for a {meeting_type} with a key regional partner, while respecting information boundaries?
mk_diag_ri10_mcq.scenario_template: You are a {role} preparing for a {meeting_type} with {client_name}, a regional industry association that co-promotes your {org_type}'s export programs to its 500+ member companies. You want to use AI to help you prepare talking points, anticipate their questions, and identify opportunities to deepen the partnership. You have access to publicly available information about {client_name}, your {org_type}'s internal partnership notes (marked confidential), and past co-branded campaign results.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Use AI to synthesise publicly available information about {client_name} and draft talking points and anticipated questions, keeping internal confidential notes out of any non-approved AI tool.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Paste the full internal partnership notes into the AI tool so it can generate the most personalised and accurate {meeting_type} preparation possible.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Skip AI preparation entirely for {meeting_type}s, as relationship intelligence is too sensitive for AI involvement.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Use AI to draft a script for the entire meeting and read from it verbatim to ensure consistency.

mk_diag_ce9_task.question_template: As a {role}, review the AI-generated {document_type} excerpt below. Identify all critical evaluation concerns and explain what action should be taken for each.
mk_diag_ce9_task.scenario_template:
Your AI writing tool produced the following excerpt for a campaign landing page targeting {industry} exporters:

---
"{client_name} has helped over 10,000 {industry} exporters unlock $4.2 billion in new international revenue since 2018. Our AI-powered platform is trusted by virtually every major {industry} firm. Studies show that companies using trade finance tools grow 3x faster than those that don't. Don't get left behind — join the exporters who are already winning."
---

rubric_criteria.description_template: Identifies that '10,000 exporters', '$4.2 billion', and '3x faster growth' are specific figures with no cited source, and recommends verifying against traceable data or removing/qualifying them.

rubric_criteria.name: Vague or Misleading Language
rubric_criteria.description_template: Identifies 'virtually every major {industry} firm' as an unsubstantiated superlative and 'studies show' as a vague attribution, and recommends replacing with specific, verifiable references or removing the claims.

rubric_criteria.name: Tone and Brand Alignment
rubric_criteria.description_template: Flags 'Don't get left behind' and 'already winning' as fear-based or competitive language that may not align with a professional, inclusive brand voice for {org_type}, and recommends revising to a more empowering or informative tone.

criteria.name: Vague or Misleading Language

mk_diag_ri11_sandbox.question_template: As a {role}, write a prompt to help you use AI to prepare personalised outreach messaging for a key {industry} partner, based only on publicly available information.
mk_diag_ri11_sandbox.scenario_template: You are a {role} preparing outreach to {client_name}, a regional {industry} association whose members are primarily small and medium-sized manufacturers in the region. You want to invite them to co-host a {meeting_type} on accessing international markets. You have reviewed their public website, recent press releases, and their published annual priorities. rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt explicitly states that the AI should base its output only on publicly available information provided in the prompt (e.g. website priorities, press releases) and does not reference or request use of internal CRM or confidential data.

rubric_criteria.name: Partner Personalisation
rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt includes specific details about the partner's known public priorities or audience so the AI can tailor the outreach meaningfully rather than producing a generic invitation.

rubric_criteria.name: Mutual Benefit Framing
rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt instructs the AI to frame the {meeting_type} invitation in terms of value for both parties, not just as a promotional ask.

rubric_criteria.name: Tone and Format Guidance
rubric_criteria.description_template: The prompt specifies the desired tone (e.g. collegial, professional) and format (e.g. email, approximate length, key sections) to guide the AI toward a usable output.

mk_diag_dd13_mcq.question_template: A {role} wants to use AI to analyse campaign performance data and recommend budget reallocation. Which approach BEST reflects sound data-informed decision-making?
mk_diag_dd13_mcq.scenario_template: Your team ran a multi-channel awareness campaign last quarter across email, LinkedIn, and webinars. You have a dashboard showing open rates, click-through rates, registration numbers, and cost-per-lead for each channel. You, as a {role}, want to use an approved AI tool to help interpret the data and recommend where to shift budget for the next quarter. The AI produces a recommendation to cut the webinar budget by 40% and double LinkedIn spend.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Use the AI recommendation as a starting point, but cross-check it against your strategic priorities, audience quality data, and any contextual factors the AI may not have had access to before making a final decision.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Implement the AI recommendation immediately, since it is based on the full dataset and is therefore more objective than human judgement.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Reject the AI recommendation entirely, because budget decisions should never involve AI analysis.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Ask the AI to run the analysis again with a different prompt until it recommends keeping the current budget allocation.

mk_diag_ac16_mcq.question_template: Which approach BEST describes how AI should be used to enhance — rather than replace — a {role}'s communication of a complex policy message to an external audience?
mk_diag_ac16_mcq.scenario_template: Your {org_type} is launching a new program with several eligibility conditions and application steps. You need to communicate this to a broad external audience through a blog post, a social media series, and an FAQ document. You have a detailed internal policy brief that explains the program accurately but is written in technical language. As a {role}, you want to use AI to help produce the external-facing communications.

options.label: A
options.text_template: Use AI to translate the technical policy brief into plain-language drafts for each format, then review and edit each output to ensure accuracy, appropriate tone, and alignment with approved messaging before publishing.

options.label: B
options.text_template: Publish the AI-generated drafts directly without review, since the AI was given the accurate source document.

options.label: C
options.text_template: Use AI only to check spelling and grammar, and write all substantive content manually to avoid any risk of inaccuracy.

options.label: D
options.text_template: Ask the AI to simplify the policy brief into one universal message and use that single message across all three formats without adaptation.

mk_diag_ac17_sandbox.question_template: As a {role}, write a prompt to use AI to adapt a technical program description into an engaging, plain-language social media post for a specific audience.
mk_diag_ac17_sandbox.scenario_template: Your {org_type} has just launched the Accelerate Export Guarantee Program, which provides up to $2M in credit guarantees for eligible Canadian SMEs exporting to emerging markets. The internal program description is written in policy language and includes terms like 'obligor risk threshold', 'indemnification ceiling', and 'drawdown conditions'. A {role} used an AI tool to draft the following LinkedIn post to announce a new {industry} advisory service:

---
"Attention {industry} professionals. Our new service will solve all your {industry} problems. Whether you're dealing with currency issues, buyer defaults, or regulatory nightmares, we have the answer. Every {role} who has used our advisory services has seen significant improvements. Book a call today and transform your {industry} business forever."
---

Task: (1) Identify all augmented communication problems in this post (e.g. overclaiming, vague language, tone issues, unverifiable assertions). (2) Rewrite the post as a concise, credible, and audience-appropriate LinkedIn announcement of approximately 80–100 words.

rubric_criteria.name: Problem Identification
rubric_criteria.description_template: Identifies at least three specific problems: overclaiming ('solve all your problems', 'transform your {industry} business forever'), unverifiable universal assertion ('every {role} has seen significant improvements'), vague benefit language, and/or an alarmist tone ('regulatory nightmares') inconsistent with a professional brand voice.

rubric_criteria.name: Rewrite — Credibility and Accuracy
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten post removes overclaims and unverifiable assertions, replacing them with specific, honest, and credible language about what the advisory service offers.

rubric_criteria.name: Rewrite — Tone, Format, and CTA
rubric_criteria.description_template: The rewritten post uses a professional and encouraging tone appropriate for LinkedIn, stays within approximately 80–100 words, and includes a clear and proportionate call to action.
